column1: # Accepted differences between our demuxers and ffprobe. Tab-separated, one rule per line:
#   format   field   scope   rule   follows   reason
# format: our container format name or *.   field: pts dts duration size pos key hash count or *.
# scope:  * | kind=video|audio|subtitle|data | codec=<ffprobe codec name> | file=<substring of the path>
# rule:   ignore | ffprobe-na (ffprobe prints N/A) | ours-na (we report no value) | tolerance=N (ticks of ffprobe's time base)
# follows: which side follows the specification (ours, ffprobe, neither), or n/a when it is a definition choice.
# A rule only excuses a difference; it is counted separately in the reports. Add rules with the experiment that justifies them.

column6: ffprobe reports the start of the Block element (id and size included); we report the start of the frame payload, as the packet's source range must be the bytes handed to the codec.
The last packet's duration: ffprobe replaces it (parser frame length for MP3/AC-3/AAC, or the edit's end); the sample table states the value we report (docs/isobmff.md).
duration-from-codec: ffprobe derives a duration the file does not store from the codec's frame length; ours stays unknown (docs/matroska-differential.md).
last-block-duration-differs: the last block's stored BlockDuration is shorter than the codec's frame; ffprobe reports the frame length (docs/matroska-differential.md).
inexact-timebase: when TimestampScale does not divide 10^9 ours are exact nanosecond ticks and ffprobe's integer time base rounds (docs/matroska-differential.md).
dts-unknown-for-video: Matroska stores presentation times only; ffprobe prints the pts as the dts (docs/matroska-differential.md).
inexact-timebase, as for pts.
inexact-timebase, as for pts.
webvtt-block-repacked: ffprobe repacks the WebVTT-in-Matroska block.
webvtt-block-repacked.
webvtt-block-repacked.
first-fragment-duration: a fragment sample whose duration comes from the tfhd default, or states 0, prints N/A in ffprobe; the box states it (docs/isobmff.md).
first-audio-run-duration: the first run states 3200 for a 1024-sample frame; ffprobe shows the frame length (docs/isobmff.md).
zero-duration-samples and first-audio-run-duration (docs/isobmff.md).
timeline-gap-deltas: 35 of 15,294 video samples have a delta far above the usual 25; ffprobe reports the usual duration (docs/isobmff.md).
negative-cts-dts-shift (docs/isobmff.md).
timeline-gap-deltas: the join of two parts has a delta above the usual one (docs/isobmff.md).
negative-cts-dts-shift: ffprobe moves DTS earlier by the largest dts - pts; we keep Pts = Dts + offset (ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.6.1.3).
negative-cts-dts-shift.
negative-cts-dts-shift.
negative-cts-dts-shift.
negative-cts-pts-shift: for fragments ffprobe moves PTS later.
negative-cts-pts-shift.
negative-cts-pts-shift.
idr-not-in-sync-table: ffprobe also marks IDR pictures the sync sample table omits; we use container information only.
idr-not-in-sync-table.
hint-track-keyframes: ffprobe marks every RTP hint packet a key frame; we report the sync table.
hint-track-keyframes.
final-empty-text-sample: the sample table ends with a zero-duration text sample (5 samples); ffprobe lists 4 (docs/isobmff.md, 3GPP TS 26.245 leaves empty samples valid).
zero-duration-samples and first-audio-run-duration: frag_every_frame writes 0 for the samples it cannot know; ffprobe reports the distance to the next sample (docs/isobmff.md).
ten-megahertz-rounding: ffprobe rounds the rescaled duration one tick away from the run's stated 10 MHz value.
video-parser-frame-timing: ffprobe takes the video packet duration from the parser's frame timing, a fixed multiple of the table's (docs/isobmff.md).
lace-shared-pts: frames of a lace without BlockDuration or DefaultDuration share the block time; ffprobe spaces them by the duration its codec parser derives (docs/matroska-differential.md).
lace-shared-pts, as for pts.
attachments-as-streams: ffprobe lists each attachment as a stream with one packet holding the file; attachments are not tracks here.
attachments-as-streams.
inexact-timebase: TimestampScale 22674 does not divide 10^9; ffprobe floors the stored DefaultDuration (26122448 ns) to a multiple of the scale (26120448 ns), ours is the stored value.

edit-list-repeats: the edit list plays part of the media twice and ffprobe lists the repeated samples again (video 1100 vs 1164) and splits PCM packets at the edit boundaries; ours lists each stored sample once (docs/isobmff.md). Positions and sizes were compared separately with the packetset command.
edit-list-repeats (mp3 track 6952 vs 7028) and the sample straddling the truncation of the corpus copy (docs/isobmff.md).

edit-list-in-fragmented-file: the edit [0+0] has segment_duration 0, which ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.6.6 reads as the whole track in a fragmented file; ffprobe drops the first 47 table samples (docs/isobmff.md).
truncated-copy-straddling-sample: ffprobe lists the sample straddling the end of the corpus copy; ours stops before it (docs/isobmff.md).
mp3-in-quicktime-one-byte-samples: the table lists the MP3 as 17.6 million one-byte samples; ffprobe reframes them by MP3 frame headers, which needs a parser at the packet level (docs/isobmff.md).
video-parser-frame-timing: packet 0 lasts 6210 in the sample table (it alternates 6210/6120); ffprobe takes the parser frame timing (docs/isobmff.md).
realaudio-deinterleave: ffprobe de-interleaves RealAudio cook/ra blocks into 280-byte packets; ours delivers the stored 1400-byte blocks (docs/matroska-differential.md).
realvideo-timestamps: ffprobe derives RealVideo frame times from the stream (azumi.mkv has blocks at 80 and 81 ms where it reports 40 and 80); ours is the block time (docs/matroska-differential.md).

no-presentation-order: an AVI index lists chunks in decode order only; for codecs with reordering (MPEG-4 Part 2 with B-frames, H.264) ffprobe prints no pts, ours is the decode-order position and equals dts (docs/avi.md).
variable-frame-audio: FLAC frames in AVI state no per-chunk duration; ffprobe prints N/A, ours is the stream header rate and scale per chunk (docs/avi.md).

dv-embedded-audio: a type 1 DV stream carries sound inside each video frame; ffprobe synthesizes audio streams from it, we expose the video track only and report the audio parameters (docs/avi.md, docs/dv.md).
dv-embedded-audio, as for type 1 AVI (docs/dv.md).
truncated-last-chunk: the cut chunk is delivered with its present bytes and the Corrupt flag; ffprobe lists an empty packet (docs/avi.md).
truncated-last-frame, as for AVI (docs/dv.md).
